SPR-S.label: he/she/it: -s missing or wrong
SPR-S.tip: He, she, it: the -s must go. She lives, he works.

SPR-DO.label: do/does in questions and negatives
SPR-DO.tip: Questions and negatives need do or does: Does she live …? He doesn't work.

SPR-USE.label: simple present for facts and routines
SPR-USE.tip: Facts and routines (always, usually, every day) take the simple present.

SP-IRREG.label: irregular past forms
SP-IRREG.tip: Some verbs have their own past form: go – went, see – saw. This stop trains them.

SP-ED.label: regular -ed forms and spelling
SP-ED.tip: Regular verbs get -ed. Watch the spelling: stop – stopped, try – tried.

SP-DID.label: did + infinitive in questions and negatives
SP-DID.tip: After did and didn't, use the infinitive: Did you see …? We didn't go.

PP-FORM.label: have/has + past participle
PP-FORM.tip: Present perfect = have/has + 3rd form: I have seen, she has swum.

PP-HAS.label: has with he/she/it
PP-HAS.tip: He, she, it: has, not have. She has never seen a shark.

PP-USE.label: present perfect with ever, never, already, yet, just
PP-USE.tip: Ever, never, already, yet, just: these words like the present perfect.

PP-SINCE.label: since vs. for
PP-SINCE.tip: Since + a point in time (since 2020), for + a period (for two years).

GOING-BE.label: am/is/are missing before going to
GOING-BE.tip: Don't forget am, is or are: We are going to help the reef.

GOING-INF.label: infinitive after going to
GOING-INF.tip: After going to comes the infinitive: going to visit, not going to visiting.

GOING-NEG.label: going to in questions and negatives
GOING-NEG.tip: Questions and negatives: Are you going to …? I'm not going to …

PROG-FORM.label: was/were + -ing
PROG-FORM.tip: Past progressive = was/were + -ing: The doctor was flying.

PROG-USE.label: background (while) vs. action (when)
PROG-USE.tip: While + past progressive is the background, when + simple past is the action that interrupts.

PP-TIME.label: present perfect with finished time (yesterday, last year, ago)
PP-TIME.tip: Yesterday, last year, ago, in 2019: finished time needs the simple past, not the present perfect.

SPPP-USE.label: choice: finished past vs. link to now
SPPP-USE.tip: Finished past: simple past. Result or experience up to now: present perfect.

TENSE-MIX.label: wrong tense for the time in the context
TENSE-MIX.tip: Look for signal words first, then choose the tense. Melbourne is a good place to practise.

W-TASK.label: task not fully answered
W-TASK.tip: Answer every part of the task.

W-FORM.label: article features (headline, intro, ending)
W-FORM.tip: An article needs a headline, an introduction and an ending.

W-PARA.label: paragraphs
W-PARA.tip: Start a new paragraph for each new idea.

W-LINK.label: linking words
W-LINK.tip: Use linking words: first, also, however, because, finally.

W-ARG.label: reasons and examples
W-ARG.tip: Give a reason and an example for each point.

W-VOC.label: vocabulary range
W-VOC.tip: Use words from the unit to make your text more interesting.

W-SPELL.label: spelling
W-SPELL.tip: Check the spelling of the unit words.

W-SENT.label: sentence structure and word order
W-SENT.tip: English word order: subject – verb – object.

G0.1: Your route starts with the basics. Every stop on the coast helps you.

G0.3: Good start! Only a few stops are on your route.
G0.4: Great check-in! You can take many express routes.

G1.1: Learn five irregular verbs a day: go – went, see – saw.
G1.2: Check the -ed spelling and the forms after did.
G1.3: Try the questions and negatives with did once more.
G1.4: Ready for the contrasts at the Coral Coast.

G2.1: Practise have/has + 3rd form with short sentences.
G2.2: Remember has for he, she and it.
G2.4: Ready for the contrast in Perth.

G3.1: Say three plans: I am going to …
G3.3: Practise questions: Are you going to …?
G3.4: You can use going to for plans and predictions.

G4.1: Practise was/were + -ing with pictures from the unit.
G4.4: Ready for the when/while story at the Coral Coast.

G5.2: Check do and does in questions.
G5.3: Use signal words like usually and every day.
G5.4: Facts and routines – no problem for you.

G6.1: Draw a time line: background first, then the action.
G6.3: Tell a short jellyfish story with when and while.
G6.4: You can tell stories in the past.

G7.1: Sort signal words: yesterday, ago – ever, never, yet.
G7.2: Finished time takes the simple past.
G7.3: Practise mixed sentences about life on a farm.
G7.4: You know when to use which past form.

G8.1: Look for signal words first, then choose the tense.
G8.2: Repeat the stop where your passport shows the fewest stars.
G8.3: Do one more mixed task in test format.
G8.4: You are ready for the test!

W1.1: Collect three ideas and one reason for each.
W1.2: Put your ideas in order: introduction, main part, ending.
W1.3: Add an example to each idea.
W1.4: Your plan is ready for the article.

W2.1: Use your plan and write one paragraph per idea.
W2.2: Add linking words and a clear ending.
W2.3: Make your text more interesting with unit words.
W2.4: Great article! Polish the details in your final draft.

W3.1: Correct one thing at a time – start with the tenses.
W3.2: Check your coach's tips one by one.
W3.3: Read your text out loud and check the flow.
W3.4: Your final draft is ready to publish.
